what: an .flv output of the tools' libx264 line (and libx265, which FFmpeg 6.1 also writes to FLV) completed with a file whose seek to the start fails: ffmpeg -ss 0 said 'could not seek to position 0.046' and decoded 0 of 90 pictures (49 of 90 for HEVC); 25 of the 26 tools of tests/sweep.py with every .mp4 output swapped for .flv wrote such a file and 23 said verified: true (loop and loudness false for a length; sphere's decoded 28). cut.py's stream copy of an MP4's B-frame H.264 into .flv did the same. -flvflags add_keyframe_index changed nothing; -bf 0 gave 90 of 90
escaped: #754 refused AVI and ASF, which store no pts, and recorded FLV as a sibling with its own cause; FLV keeps its pts, so ffprobe reads every frame's time, and no check of these tools seeks into the file. No test wrote an FLV of a re-encode or read one back after a seek, and no test ran every tool into every container
mechanism: runner._CONTAINER_ENCODERS has an .flv entry that refuses the H.264/HEVC encoders before ffmpeg runs, dry runs included, and shares the AVI hint, so runner._copies_reordered_video() refuses a stream copy of B-frame video into it from another container. The class has its guard: test_guards.CapabilityGuard runs every tool of the sweep's table as a dry run into twelve containers and reads back each container and encoder pair the completed runs plan (frames after -ss 0, stream lengths)
